pages.text: "Sunlight is making a square on the paper door." Grandma called from outside the room in her gray layered clothes. Little fox Yuki pulled the quilt over their head.
"I want to see the white frost. In a little while..." Yuki gripped the quilt and closed their eyes again. The room grew brighter.
Much later, Yuki went into the yard and looked down. The grass was wet and shiny; all the white frost had melted. "...It all melted." Yuki pressed their lips shut.
Back inside, Grandma sat beside Yuki. "Getting out of the quilt isn't hard. Stretch your body when your eyes open." She held a wrist and lifted the arm high.
Yuki stretched both arms overhead and lifted their heels. As their body grew longer, sleepiness slipped out through fingertips and toes. "Sunlight on the Door—Stretch!" Yuki's eyes brightened.
"After stretching, open the door. Morning is waiting." Yuki slid the paper door open with both hands. Cool air drifted in.
In the yard, brown dog Momo tilted their head and barked. Yuki opened both arms at the porch's edge. "Hello, morning! Sunlight on the Door—Stretch!"
Last came washing. Yuki scooped basin water onto their face. Cold water ran down their cheeks, washing away the last sleepiness. "I opened the morning by myself today!"

The next day, as the paper door brightened, Yuki opened their eyes first. "One, stretch long! Two, open the door and say hello! Three, wash with cold water!" Yuki pushed away the quilt and fixed the scarf knot.
White frost covered every blade of grass! Grandma lifted Yuki into a hug. Some morning sights could only be seen by getting up early. "Grandma, Sunlight on the Door—Stretch!"
